t1.descripcion:
The present perfect is formed with:

HABER (present) + participle of the verb

Conjugation of HABER:
• yo HE
• tú HAS
• él/ella/usted HA
• nosotros HEMOS
• vosotros HABÉIS
• ellos/ellas/ustedes HAN

Regular participles:
• -AR → -ADO: hablado, estudiado, trabajado, cantado, bailado
• -ER → -IDO: comido, bebido, corrido, leído, aprendido
• -IR → -IDO: vivido, escrito, recibido, abierto, partido

🔹 EXAMPLES:
• Yo he hablado con María. (I have spoken with María)
• Tú has comido paella. (You have eaten paella)
• Ella ha vivido en Madrid. (She has lived in Madrid)
• Nosotros hemos estudiado. (We have studied)
• Ellos han llegado tarde. (They have arrived late)

📌 STRUCTURE: HABER + participle

❌ COMMON MISTAKE:
Don't forget to conjugate HABER correctly according to the person. Don't say "Yo ha hablado" (incorrect). Say "Yo he hablado".

t2.descripcion:
Most common irregular participles:

🔹 LIST OF IRREGULAR PARTICIPLES:

• abrir → abierto (open)
• cubrir → cubierto (covered)
• decir → dicho (said)
• escribir → escrito (written)
• hacer → hecho (done/made)
• morir → muerto (died)
• poner → puesto (put)
• romper → roto (broken)
• ver → visto (seen)
• volver → vuelto (returned)
• freír → frito (fried)
• resolver → resuelto (solved)
• devolver → devuelto (returned)
• descubrir → descubierto (discovered)

🔹 EXAMPLES:
• He abierto la puerta. (I have opened the door)
• ¿Has visto la película? (Have you seen the movie?)
• Ella ha escrito una carta. (She has written a letter)
• Hemos hecho la tarea. (We have done the homework)
• El花瓶 se ha roto. (The vase has broken)

📌 TRICK TO REMEMBER:
Most irregular participles end in -to, -so, -cho:
• -to: abierto, cubierto, muerto, roto
• -so: puesto, impreso
• -cho: dicho, hecho

❌ COMMON MISTAKE:
Do not confuse the irregular participle "hecho" with the adjective "hecho" (done). In the present perfect, the participle is always used.

t4.descripcion:
🔹 KEY DIFFERENCES:

| Aspect | Present Perfect | Simple Past |
|---------|-------------------|---------------------|
| Temporality | Recent past / relevant today | Distant past / completed |
| Markers | hoy, esta semana, este año, ya, todavía no | ayer, la semana pasada, el año pasado |
| Example | He comido hoy | Comí ayer |
| Experience | He visitado París (en mi vida) | Visité París en 2019 |

🔹 COMPARATIVE EXAMPLES:

• Hoy he desayunado a las 8. (today - perfecto)
• Ayer desayuné a las 7. (yesterday - indefinido)

• Esta semana he trabajado mucho. (this week - perfecto)
• La semana pasada trabajé mucho. (last week - indefinido)

• ¿Has visto la última película de Almodóvar? (perfecto)
• Viste la película conmigo el mes pasado. (indefinido)

📌 IN SPAIN:
The present perfect is very common, even for actions from today or this week.

📌 IN LATIN AMERICA:
The simple past is used more, even for recent actions.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE:
Do not use the present perfect with "el año pasado". Use the simple past.

t3.descripcion:
The present perfect is used for:

🔹 1. PAST EXPERIENCES (without specifying when):
   • He visitado París. (I have visited Paris)
   • ¿Has probado la paella? (Have you tried paella?)
   • Nunca he estado en China. (I have never been to China)

🔹 2. RECENT ACTIONS (with "acabar de"):
   • Acabo de terminar. (I have just finished)
   • Hemos llegado hace cinco minutos. (We arrived five minutes ago)

🔹 3. ACTIONS WITHOUT A SPECIFIC TIME (with time markers):
   • Hoy he trabajado mucho. (Today I have worked a lot)
   • Esta semana he estudiado español. (This week I have studied Spanish)
   • Este año he viajado tres veces. (This year I have traveled three times)

🔹 4. WITH YA, TODAVÍA NO, NUNCA, ALGUNA VEZ:
   • Ya he comido. (I have already eaten)
   • Todavía no he visto la película. (I haven't seen the movie yet)
   • ¿Alguna vez has viajado a Europa? (Have you ever traveled to Europe?)

📌 TYPICAL TIME MARKERS:

| Marker | Meaning | Example |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| ya | already | Ya he comido |
| todavía no | not yet | Todavía no he salido |
| nunca | never | Nunca he visto eso |
| alguna vez | ever | ¿Alguna vez has ido? |
| hoy | today | Hoy he trabajado |
| esta semana | this week | Esta semana he estudiado |
| este mes | this month | Este mes he viajado |
| este año | this year | Este año he aprendido |

❌ COMMON MISTAKE:
Do not use the present perfect with "ayer", "la semana pasada" or other expressions of completed past time. For that, the preterite is used.

Afterwards, I ate with friends at a Chinese restaurant. We ate a lot! In the afternoon I watched a Spanish movie and then went home. I haven't done my Spanish homework yet. And you? Have you finished your homework yet? Have you ever seen a Spanish movie?

dict.在西班牙，饭前去喝开胃酒很常见。人们和朋友或家人去酒吧，喝点饮料，配一份小吃。你: In Spain, it's common to go for an aperitif before a meal. People go to a bar with friends or family, have a drink, and have a tapa. Have you ever tried tapas? Have you ever been to a Spanish bar? The aperitif is a social moment, not just for eating but also for chatting and enjoying.
dict.在中国，朋友聚会常去餐馆直接吃饭，而西班牙人喜欢在饭前先去酒吧吃小吃。这种习惯与: In China, friends often go to a restaurant to eat directly, while Spaniards like to go to a bar for tapas before a meal. This habit has similarities with some pre-meal snack cultures in China, but the form is different.
dict.现在完成时的结构是 haber + 过去分词，不能用现在时动词。正确形式是 he: The structure of the present perfect is haber + past participle; you cannot use a present tense verb. The correct form is he hablado.
dict.动词 hacer 的过去分词是不规则的：hecho，不是 heco。: The past participle of the verb hacer is irregular: hecho, not heco.
dict.已经表示“还没有”，不能再加“ya”，语义重复。: 已经 means 'not yet', so you cannot add 'ya'; it would be redundant.
dict.与明确的过去时间（ayer）连用时，西班牙语通常用简单过去时，不用现在完成时。: When used with a specific past time (ayer), Spanish usually uses the simple past, not the present perfect.
dict.这个句子是正确的，但常见错误是漏掉过去分词的性数一致？实际上，现在完成时中过去分: This sentence is correct, but a common mistake is omitting the gender/number agreement of the past participle? Actually, in the present perfect the past participle does not change with the object; here it is correct. Another common mistake is 'he escribido', which should be 'he escrito'.
